caseObservations.observed: The material gives candidate actions but the task still requires explaining three concrete effects, comparing consequences and constructing a workable plan. The changed deadline/no-takeover condition requires adapting support to listening/organisation. The 4+4+2 rubric rewards reasons and adaptation rather than copying a label.

The belonging/self-protection conflict requires justification; the solution attributes responsibility for pressure to those applying it. The online-team transfer changes the social demand and requires boundaries and support. The 4+4+2 rubric preserves privacy and avoids diagnosis.

Equal gaming duration deliberately removes duration as the discriminator. The comparison rests on control and functional consequences. The single longer planned occasion tests persistent pattern versus isolated episode, rather than numerical substitution. No clinical diagnosis or personal disclosure is asserted.

Music enjoyment and continued substance use with adverse consequences change the object of evaluation. The moral label must be refuted without diagnosing D or prescribing withdrawal. The privacy transfer retains the information limit. Detailed solutions are author material and cannot be treated as independent learner performances.

visualObservations.observed: Each full page shows the complete goal ID, title, description, six-jurisdiction scope and external prerequisite without clipping. Main learner and four separate thought scenes show conversation, outdoor movement, music and scheduling. The foreground notebook is lined and blank, usable from the learner position. At 360 and 680 px the four main actions remain distinguishable without required small text. These are possible coping examples, not evidence of the learner performance or guaranteed prevention.

The page views preserve the whole ID, title, description, six-jurisdiction scope, external health prerequisite and external addiction-development successor. At original, 360 and 680 px the left scenes show social connection/putting phone aside/rest, while the right repeated arrows, nighttime use and desk distraction suggest patterns worth questioning. The central question and supportive person prevent a binary diagnosis reading. The illustrative clock is not a shared duration measurement or diagnostic cutoff; matching alt text explicitly prevents that inference.
